BrandMotif

The official "cubo impossível" motif — the brand's central visual idea, supplied by Sesc as vector artwork and split into six constructions. Defaults to one brand family per shape; hue="original" retains supplied colours. Never re-maps per theme. Invalid variants/hues return null.

Live example

The example needs JavaScript; the usage below shows the markup.

Usage

BrandMotif — cubo impossível

The official motif — the brand's central visual idea (reach, expansion, flexibility, lateral thinking), supplied by Sesc as vector artwork and split into its six constructions. This replaces the geometric placeholder that shipped earlier.

<BrandMotif variant="cube" size={240} />
<BrandMotif variant="interlock" size={320} opacity={0.35} />   // behind a hero
<BrandMotif variant="chain" size={200} title="Motivo institucional da Rede" />
<BrandMotif variant="cube" hue="purple" size={240} />          // restated in another family
variantdefault brand huesupplied huewhat it is
cubepurplegreenthe solid isometric cube — the base mark
interlockbluebluetwo cubes passing through each other
bargreengreena cube pierced by a bar that could not pass through it
framepinkpinkan open frame with two impossible voids
chainorangepinka zig-zag chain of bars, the widest construction
hollowyellowbluea cube opened out around a hollow centre

hue accepts green, blue, pink, purple, orange, yellow, or original. Omit it for the distinct brand family assigned above. These six default treatments are derived palette remaps. hue="original" restores the exact supplied fills. The source SVG assets stay untouched. motifDefaultHues exports the assignments for consumers and the showcase.

Rules

  • One focal construction per composition, in negative space (corner of a band, beside a section eyebrow), at 25% or less of the composition. Two competing motifs read as decoration and lose the meaning.
  • The geometry belongs to the artwork; the hue is a choice. A motif never re-maps per theme, exactly like the logo. hue="original" renders the exact fills Sesc supplied. Sesc's sheet only covers green, blue and pink, so hue is how purple, orange and yellow are reached — ramps come from the manual's published palette, never from sampling the artwork, and the remap keeps each face's luminance rank so the solid still reads as a solid. Say "derived" when it matters: those three hues are ours, not supplied, and official artwork should replace them if it arrives.
  • The signature geometry stays exactly as supplied: never redraw, rotate, stretch, distort or animate one. Generated shapes and motion are not drawn here; they come only from the motif engine, through MotifPattern (fields) and MotifLoader (transient loading). A pattern is a field, not a construction, and the loader is exempt from the one-focal rule. Generated shapes are derived, not supplied by Sesc.
  • Drop opacity to ~0.3 when it sits behind content, and never place text on the cube faces or on pattern cells (use a solid panel).
  • It is not a logo: it never substitutes for the selo, nor sits beside it in a lockup.
  • For a full-bleed field of cubes rather than one construction, use the official pattern backgrounds in assets/patterns/ as a CSS background image — see docs/recipes.md.

Decorative by default (aria-hidden); pass title in pt-BR only when the motif carries meaning on its own.

BrandMotif.js is generated by scripts/build-motifs.mjs from assets/motifs/cubes-official.svg — edits to it are overwritten.

Props

PropTypeRequiredNotes
variantMotifVariant—Which official construction to render (default 'cube')
sizenumber—Rendered square size in px (default 240)
titlestring—Accessible label. Omit when decorative (rendered aria-hidden)
opacitynumber—Fade the motif when it sits behind content (default 1)
huegreen blue pink purple orange yellow original—Omit for the assigned brand family; "original" preserves supplied fills; a palette family selects a derived remap.

CSS classes

Renders no class contract of its own (generated artwork or a function library).
